deadline_producer_20261012.cpu_observation: Producer consumed approximately one CPU core; reader approximately 0.39 core.
deadline_producer_20261012.limitation: One ten-minute run passed; normal scheduling previously overran at 298 seconds. Source ring retains under 1 ms of headroom at the worst observed backlog. No indefinite or system-load-independent guarantee.

live_controls_20261012.status: passed on both native SoapySDR ABI and distribution GNU Radio gr-soapy
live_controls_20261012.semantics: A live hardware setting change stops and restarts capture, discards queued old samples, returns one SOAPY_SDR_OVERFLOW with HAS_TIME, and rebases software timestamps by measured host pause duration. Settled segments remain continuous. No-op/invalid settings do not interrupt reception.
live_controls_20261012.rollback: Intentional iw rejection at 40 MS/s restored the old frequency/rate and resumed after one explicit discontinuity.
live_controls_20261012.remaining: Hardware tuning still restricted to 5 MHz grid; no sample-accurate timestamps across tuning, no AGC/gain controls or normal-user lifecycle yet.

fine_tuning_20261012.status: Fine tuning verified; full receiver remains experimental with RF-quality failures unresolved
fine_tuning_20261012.digital_translation: Nearest 5 MHz RF center, negative complex mixing at native sample rate before decimation. Oscillator phase, FIR history and timestamps persist through same-RF-center updates; crossing RF centers reports an interruption.

faults_and_changes.allocation_fault: ret=-110 at allocation; completed DMA, recording LA, 258 packets. RX queue starvation inferred, not proved. Deadline-task wiphy yield now sleeps 25..50 us every ~2 ms; API transition sequence passed afterward. HRTICK/HRTICK_DL disabled on this host.
faults_and_changes.trigger_semantics: 255 now used for all modes after 20 MS/s zero-count early completion; exact hardware semantics remain unproved.

image_observation.stage: before-concurrent20 in first priority-lock fine test

rf_anomalies.status: Unresolved intermittent receive-quality failure after hardware mode changes. Could involve gain, calibration, tap/format or clock state; physical ADC saturation is not yet established.

limitations: Digital translation shifts the existing RF passband; it does not widen or recenter the analogue filter.
Fine changes cause a normal FIR settling transient but no sample-count gap. Hardware center/rate changes interrupt acquisition.
Gain/AGC, image/clipping cause, longer robustness, broader RF coverage, installation and Gqrx/SDR++ testing remain.

notes: Periodic RF windows do not prove phase continuity of every sample.
AGC disable, ADC FIFO reset, source3, pre-tune SMALLBW restoration were isolated experiments; none eliminated RF faults.
Pluto simultaneous RX reference supports locating strong-image fault to Realtek side.

ring_size_experiment_20261012.tone_probe_result: First five 64KiB regions recovered tone at 56.48..56.75dB peak/median; sixth region did not recover it (10.89dB).
ring_size_experiment_20261012.interpretation: All higher size codes behave as 320KiB; suggests LA engine saturates size at 320KiB despite register accepting codes. This is empirical, not a datasheet maximum claim.
ring_size_experiment_20261012.experimental_clock8_note: Exploratory clock8 run was not a slow clock; measured wrap timing was consistent with an unqualified ~80M raw-record/s fallback. Final all-selector results use qualified clock4.

fast_dma_80_160_20261012.result: 80 and160 MS/s continuous reception failed;40 MS/s control passed
experiments: C++ raw reader with SCHED_DEADLINE producer
two idle IDDMA channels copying disjoint halves of each packet
fast_dma_80_160_20261012.interpretation: No useful throughput increase. Host FIFOs had zero drops, but source backlog exceeded40960 records. Parallel-channel timings suggest a shared bottleneck, not proof of its physical location. Short native80/160 RF captures contain the Pluto tone; these do not qualify full-band fidelity or continuity.
fast_dma_80_160_20261012.cleanup: Pluto attributes and original TX powerdown restored by finally; temporary modules, firmware and NM config removed; original working driver hash unchanged.

other_tests.clock_selectors: AFE_CTRL1 exposed DMAC and DCPU clock selectors0..3 read back, but did not improve copy speed. Original0x1fffff1f restored. Actual selected frequency not established.

other_tests.PAXIDMA: Located live engine at0x18006000 and8-byte TXBDs in firmware SRAM. Uninitialized channel2 probe using producer-owned descriptor memory timed out with index0,busy0 and zero host bytes. This is not a working bypass. Firmware-owned channels0/1 were not replaced.

A faster packet AXI path or a ring-to-PCIe route avoiding IDDMA remains unresolved.

frequency_coverage_2026_10_12.method: Two Pluto tones at +500/-500 kHz; native 20 MS/s packed signed int8 IQ, path1/source2/format14. Correct 1MHz movement and >30dB peak/median required. Each verified center also tested with 100ms PCIe stream.
limitations: All advertised channel centers surveyed for tune acceptance; RF tone checks only at listed verified centers.
Pluto LO limited to 6GHz; reception above 6GHz is not RF qualified.
Channel-center coverage is not continuous off-band tuning or a measured passband edge.
Narrow tones and short streaming tests do not establish sensitivity, full-band fidelity or long-run continuity.
Soapy plugin remains restricted to 2.4GHz; these measurements use low-level capture helpers.
